top_categories.workout_context: 6,289ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gruyère Cycling Tour's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before September.

Road-specific control matters at Gruyère Cycling Tour. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 70 miles.
89ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Gruyère Cycling Tour, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gruyère Cycling Tour. Train it until it feels boring.
6,289ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
70 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gruyère Cycling Tour. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Base fitness for Gruyère Cycling Tour. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Low-cadence force work supports 6,289ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.weather: September in Charmey, Fribourg, Switzerland. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Gruyère Cycling Tour. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan for Gruyère Cycling Tour's 70 miles. Start early and use products you tolerate. Use the organizer's current resupply plan for final carry decisions.
race_overlay.altitude: Gruyère Cycling Tour includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Gruyère Cycling Tour rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.
